Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

with the courier and the box belongs in the archive cabinet", "output": "For the rehearsal archive, I want to set up a listening and transfer session for the west hall recording from the spring company run, and I need the original reel brought to B59 before the technician starts the playback check. Please keep the reel in its labeled box until the table is clear, and do not wind it onto the smaller machine just to see whether it fits the hub. That machine is for the interview cassettes, and its take-up spindle has been sticking since Monday. The room booking starts at 10:30 on Thursday, but the courier can leave the box at the desk from 9:15 if someone signs for it. I can arrive at 9:40 with the new inventory sheet and the cotton gloves, and I will check the accession number against the paper sleeve before anything is opened.

Bram is the second person on the session and should handle the playback notes while I check the physical condition of the reel. Please tell him that the first pass is for listening only and that we should not pause to label every breath or chair noise on the track. We need to note the slate at the beginning, the music cue at about twelve minutes, and the stretch of room tone near the end. If the counters on the old player drift, we can write down the displayed time and the spoken slate rather than guessing at an exact tape position. Bram has listened to this company before, but he has not heard this particular recording, so let him take his own first impressions before he reads the old catalog card. The card may help with names, but it should not decide what he hears. I will bring two sharpened pencils because the archive pens have left marks on the sleeves, and one blank listening log for each of us.

Please include a short instruction on the door that says, “Recording review in progress. Please wait outside until invited in.” We will have the tabletop recorder running only during the playback and will switch it off for conversation so the room sound does not get mixed into the archive copy. The small red lamp above the door is unreliable and must not be treated as a sign that recording is active. Someone should check the recorder display and say aloud whether the counter is moving before we begin. If the display stays blank, we should stop there and ask the equipment desk for help rather than trying a different power supply from the drawer. The drawer has adapters for several units, and the labels are not all readable. I can bring the known cable from the archive cabinet, but only if it is returned there after the session and marked on the checkout card. We should keep drinks on the low shelf outside the work area, even if the room feels warm, because the reel box needs to stay dry and the table has no raised edge.

1. Before the first playback, check the label on the box against the accession sheet and record any difference without correcting the label.
2. Confirm that both listening logs show the date, the room, and the names of the people present.
3. Listen once all the way through without stopping, then compare notes and choose the points that need a second listen.
4. Make a transfer only if the playback is stable and the equipment desk has confirmed the archive recorder is set to the agreed level. If the reel slows or makes a scraping sound, stop the machine and leave the tape where it is. Do not rewind it to test the sound. We can put a note in the log and ask the preservation technician to inspect it later. This is not a repair session, and we should not try to clean the reel ourselves, even if there is dust visible through the box window.

When we reach the music cue, I want to mark its approximate position and write down the words used in the slate if they are clear. If they are not clear, leave a question mark in the listening log and note which of us heard the uncertain word rather than filling it in from memory. The company names in the older finding aid were typed from a handwritten list, and two surnames may be misspelled, so we should keep the sound and the catalog spelling separate until the archivist can compare them with the program. The sound of a page turning is part of the recording and does not need a separate technical fault note. The short burst of static after the music cue does need to be marked because it may affect the transfer later. Please do not add an estimate of its cause; we do not know whether it came from the source reel or the old playback deck.

After the first pass, we can take ten minutes to compare the logs and agree on the time points for another listen. If we disagree about a word, put both versions in the margin with our initials and leave the final choice to the archivist. This is especially important for the names because a confident guess can look like a verified identification when it is copied into the catalog. The transfer file should use the date and accession number in its working name and stay in the review folder until the archivist checks it. Do not send a copy to the company or upload it to the public catalog as part of this session. The recording agreement allows staff review, but the release status still needs to be checked before any outside sharing. If the file is too large for the review folder, we should ask the digital archivist which temporary location to use instead of splitting it into pieces on our own.

At the end, please return the reel to its box with the leader visible and place the box on the padded cart, not on the shelf by the door. Put the logs and the checkout card in the blue folder and leave that folder in the locked cabinet for the archivist to collect. If the session runs past noon, call the front desk to keep the room reserved rather than leaving the equipment unattended. The next group is scheduled at one and may need time to set up the chairs, so we should leave the table clear and put the two pencils back in the top drawer after checking that neither has touched the tape. If the courier has not yet taken the empty transport case back, note that on the desk sheet and do not leave it beside the reel box. The case belongs with the courier, and the box belongs in the archive cabinet."}]
